title: Potato and Onion Vareniki with Sour Cream
summary: Soft hand-folded dumplings filled with mashed potato, onion and cottage cheese, boiled and finished with butter, sour cream and dill.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
floury potatoes, peeled, in 3 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (1%)
ingredients.note: about 6.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Melt the butter into the hot water, then stir the mixture into the flour and salt, followed by the beaten egg. Knead for 5-6 minutes until the dough turns smooth and soft.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes. This relaxes the gluten so it rolls out thin later without shrinking back or tearing.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a pan of cold water with a pinch of salt and boil for 15-20 minutes, until very tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry for 2 minutes, which drives off excess moisture before mashing.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, cook the chopped onions in 40 g of butter in a large frying pan over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until soft and golden.

steps.title: Mash and cool the filling
steps.text: Mash the potatoes with two-thirds of the cooked onions, the cottage cheese, salt and pepper, then leave the mixture to cool completely - filling a dough while it's still warm makes the dough sticky and prone to tearing. Keep the remaining onions aside for topping later.

steps.title: Shape the vareniki
steps.text: Roll out half the dough to 2 mm thick and cut rounds with an 8 cm cutter. Put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre of each round, fold it into a half-moon, and pinch the edges firmly from one end to the other, pressing out any trapped air as you go - air left inside will make them burst as they cook. Re-roll the scraps once and repeat with the remaining dough; you should get about 30 vareniki in total.

steps.title: Cook the vareniki
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 40 g salt, then lower to a gentle boil. Cook the vareniki in 3 batches: once they float, cook for 2-3 minutes more, until the dough at the pinched edges is tender. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Toss the cooked vareniki with the butter, then serve topped with the reserved onions, sour cream and chopped dill.

tips: Let the filling cool completely before shaping - warm filling softens the dough and makes it tear or stick to your hands.
Pinch the edges firmly all the way along each dumpling, pressing out trapped air, since any air pocket left inside tends to make them split open in the water.
Cook the vareniki in batches rather than all at once, so they have room to float freely and cook evenly without sticking together.
Rest the dough for the full 30 minutes - skipping this makes it spring back and shrink as you try to roll it thin.
storage: Uncooked, shaped vareniki can be frozen on a tray then bagged for up to 2 months and cooked straight from frozen, adding a minute or two to the time. Cooked vareniki keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently in a pan with a little butter until piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
